request: Add a waitlist to our class booking app so full classes don't turn people away.

nuances.nuance: What happens when a spot opens: automatic promotion, or an offer the person must accept within a stated window.
The order the waitlist is served in (join time), how ties resolve, and whether any membership tier or staff override jumps the queue.
A person on the waitlist for two classes that overlap in time: promoting one must resolve the other.
The no-show or late-cancellation policy that already exists: whether a declined or missed promotion counts against it.
Promotion is triggered by a cancellation that happens outside the person's session, so it is background work with a stated trigger and timeliness.
Notification of a promotion: the channel, what it says, and what happens when sending fails.
Two spots opening at once, or two cancellations at the same moment: no double promotion and no over-booked class.
A waitlisted person booking directly at the same moment a promotion is offered to them.
Payment for a promoted booking: when it is taken and what happens when it fails.
A cap on the waitlist itself, and what a person sees when even the waitlist is full.
A cut-off before class start after which no promotion happens.
Staff raising or lowering a class's capacity while a waitlist exists.
The class being cancelled entirely: what happens to everyone waiting.
The waitlist entry as a record with its join time and state, and whether a position is stored or derived.
What becomes of waitlist entries after the class has run, and how long they are kept.
What a member can see of the waitlist: their own position, and not other people's identities.
Staff can see the waitlist, promote or remove someone by hand, and see who was promoted when.
The feature can be turned off, or enabled per class or class type.
A bound on how soon a promotion follows a cancellation.
A class that is not full still books directly as it does today, and existing bookings are unaffected.
Classes that are already full when the feature ships: whether they gain a waitlist and how.

request: Set up automatic reminders for unpaid invoices.

nuances.nuance: The schedule: how many reminders and at what offsets from the due date, including whether any are sent before it.
Every condition that stops the sequence: paid, part-paid, voided, credited, disputed, or on a payment plan.
A part-paid invoice: whether the reminder states the remaining balance rather than the original amount.
An existing do-not-contact, paused or unsubscribed state on the customer, and whether a billing notice is exempt from a marketing opt-out.
Idempotency: the same reminder is never sent twice, including after a retry, a redeploy or two schedulers running.
A check at the moment of sending that the invoice is still unpaid, not only when the batch was selected.
The send failing: retry policy, a provider outage, and escalation to a person when it keeps failing.
The sending provider's rate limit and how a large batch is paced within it.
Invoices already overdue when the feature is switched on: the whole backlog of reminders does not go out at once.
Time zone and sending hours: the customer's local time, business hours, weekends and holidays.
Currency and amount formatting for the recipient.
A bouncing or invalid recipient address, and an invoice with no contact at all.
More than one billing contact, and which of them is written to.
A record per invoice per reminder step, showing what was sent and when, visible on the invoice.
What the reminder contains: invoice reference, amount, due date and a way to pay, and whether that link expires.
Who may configure the schedule and who may send or stop a reminder by hand.
Turning it off globally and per customer, previewing or dry-running it, and resending by hand.
Seeing what the system will send next and what it failed to send.
A bound on sending volume or on how late a scheduled reminder may go out.
Nothing changes about how invoices are created, paid or recorded.
